title: Curriculum and Planning (TS2-TS7)
journeyNote: This is where observing turned into doing. What began as paperwork became lessons I delivered to two sections.
overview: Where planning became practice. Compilation of verified daily lesson logs, competency matrices, classroom management plans, instructional materials, and assessment instruments delivered across two high school sections.

taskSheets.title: Annotated DLL
taskSheets.fullTitle: Task Sheet 2: Annotated Daily Lesson Log
taskSheets.opener: Creating a Daily Lesson Log requires precise alignment with the MATATAG curriculum and the Budget of Work (BOW).
taskSheets.reflection: Annotating showed me that alignment is everything: topic, objectives, discussion, and assessment must all point to the same place. It wasn't confusing, but it was demanding to plan, because I can't write an objective I can't actually teach and assess. Now, I write the assessment in my head before I write the objective.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: DLL has complete parts, clear reference to MATATAG Curriculum and complies with AI Declaration policy. Content and performance standards exactly match the BOW.

taskSheets.title: Competencies Alignment
taskSheets.opener: Mapping out competencies ensures every objective directly supports the prescribed curriculum guide.
taskSheets.reflection: I began by studying the lesson: the exemplar, the Budget of Work, the Curriculum Guide, and outside research on the content. I drafted my CAP objectives, built a student-centered activity to meet them, and when something did not line up, I adjusted the objectives, the activity, or the assessment until all three landed at the same place.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: The output shows that most objectives are accurately aligned with the BOW/CG/MELCS competencies. The competency and objectives are clear.

taskSheets.title: Classroom Management Plan
taskSheets.opener: Establishing a safe and organized classroom environment relies on consistent routines and clear expectations.
taskSheets.reflection: What I noticed first in my CT's class was her loud, well-modulated voice, which I want to adopt. I also learned from her slides that clear visuals matter, since text that is cut off or overlapping can distract an audience. For positive behavior, I implemented a Token Economy paired with Behavior-Specific Praise, where tokens could be redeemed for privileges. For negative behavior, I applied logical, consistent, and non-punitive consequences like temporary loss of privileges.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: Rules established are clear, clearly explains specific and consistent routines, routines are realistic.

taskSheets.title: Daily Lesson Log
taskSheets.opener: Structuring the week's lessons breaks down complex topics into digestible daily competencies.
taskSheets.reflection: Looking at my logs, I noticed the weekly rhythm: Day 1 introduces the topic, Days 2 to 4 deepen it with activities, and the last day generalizes the lesson and adds one more activity so learners retain it.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: Intentions are clearly stated with KSA per session. Learning competencies show what learners will work on, relevant to real life.

taskSheets.title: Lesson Plans and Instructional Materials
taskSheets.fullTitle: Task Sheet 6: Lesson Plans and Instructional Materials
taskSheets.opener: Detailed lesson plans serve as the blueprint for engaging discussions and effective instructional materials.
taskSheets.reflection: I am proudest of two things I built. The first is a fish-hook web app where learners appear as swimming fish and I "hook" one at random to recite. The second is a peso-bill reward system with bills of 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, and 1,000, each in three designs with an animal and a quote. Learners earned bills based on the quality of their answers. This is where my programming background and my teaching met.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: The daily lesson log shows clear and complete sequence of learning objective.

taskSheets.title: Assessment Tools and Evaluation
taskSheets.fullTitle: Task Sheet 7: Assessment Tools and Evaluation
taskSheets.opener: Building assessments requires testing practical relevance and higher-order thinking, not just rote memory.
taskSheets.reflection: Fairness and accuracy matter because assessment represents the quality of a learner's work. Learners come to school to learn, and if the assessment is poorly built, that goal is not met. I built a multiple-choice contextual exam using real-world food service scenarios. I learned that clear formatting and shading indicators significantly help students understand what is expected.
taskSheets.ctFeedback: Assess Higher Order Thinking Skills, contextual and practical relevance (uses real world industry and scenarios), uses multiple choice options and shading indicators... TOS contents are aligned with the Test.
